Nasdaq Composite, meanwhile, pulled back 2% on Thursday, dragged down by players including Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia and Google.

El-Erian pointed to investors selling other holdings to fund the large Anthropic offering, an effect he termed comparable to rising financing costs when major borrowers enter markets without a reduction in overall demand.

Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management called the expectation for Anthropic IPO lifting the broader AI trade a case of "classic groupthink."

Shares of Claude parent Anthropic PBC closed 17% higher on its first day of trading on the Nasdaq, even as the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite index pulled back sharply—a move Mohamed El-Erian described as the market "making room" for AI.

"...remember this isn't just about the promise of AI, but about making room for it," El-Erian wrote in a post on X.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

The Wharton professor and economist said investors sold other stocks to free up money for the big Anthropic offering. He compared it to what happens in bond markets when large new borrowers appear without others pulling back, pushing financing costs higher for everyone.

Source: Mohamed El-Erian/ X

Meanwhile, Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management called the expectation for Anthropic IPO lifting the broader AI trade a case of "classic groupthink."

"My take: Today's action isn't an indictment of AI. It's what happens when many were on the same side of the trade. Investors still want the exposure, and the $80B Anthropic raised will soon fund infrastructure and applications," Munster said.

Source: Gene Munster/ X
Anthropic's $83 Offering Tops SpaceX As Biggest IPO On Record

Anthropic priced its offering at $83 a share on Wednesday, above the marketed range of $70 to $78. It sold 980 million Class A shares, raising $81.3 billion—the largest IPO on record, ahead of SpaceX's June listing. A simultaneous $26 billion private placement involving Nvidia, Microsoft, Google and others brought total proceeds to about $107 billion. At the IPO price, the company carried a fully diluted valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion.

Shares opened on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT and opened at a 34% premium to the offer price, implying a market value near $2 trillion. The stock reached an intraday high near $115 before easing and closed at $97.17, up 17% from the IPO price. Nasdaq Composite, meanwhile, pulled back 2.25%, dragged down by players including Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia and Google.

Nebius (NBIS) stock's Q3 sell-off looks like an attractive opportunity, with shares down almost 64% from their 52-week high. The artificial intelligence (AI) cloud infrastructure provider disappointed investors with another capacity delay, but the underlying business momentum tells a very different story. Rather than pulling back, customers are locking in much larger, multi-year commitments. As CEO Arkady Volozh emphasized on the earnings call, "The demand for AI is real and substantial."

Q3 2026 revenue surged 571%, and new contract economics improved. I understand the concerns about financing this enormous expansion. Yet customers' willingness to help fund it makes me more confident. Thus, I rate NBIS stock a Buy.

A Strong Quarter Got Overshadowed

Nebius' strong Q3 results got overshadowed by another capacity delay. Investors were already questioning Neocloud financing and the sustainability of AI spending. Nebius then shifted some expected revenue into early 2027 because third-party capacity was delayed. Management now expects 2026 revenue near the low end of its $3.0–$3.4 billion range.

Its $7 billion-plus annualized revenue milestone moves from December to February. That is disappointing, although the customer contracts behind the delayed capacity remain intact.

More importantly, the company showed considerable progress. Revenue reached $980.8 million, up 68% sequentially, while AI Cloud revenue grew 643% year-over-year. Group adjusted EBITDA reached $465.8 million, and AI Cloud's adjusted EBITDA margin was 53.2%. Annualized revenue run rate rose 113% sequentially to $6.4 billion.

Q3 included $325 million of nonrecurring partner revenue. Excluding that contribution, revenue still exceeded four times last year's total. Customers have also signed over $12 billion of contract value since Q3 began.

The improving contract terms are what impressed me most. Prepayments on Q3 contracts lasting at least a year covered more than 100% of associated capex. That compares with 50%–60% in Q2. Management's revenue-based payback estimate for comparable contracts improved to 19 months from 22 months. Customers are signing longer agreements at higher prices, helping Nebius recover its spending faster.
